answer:
Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) to solve a 2D plane-stress linear elasticity problem on a rectangular plate.
The domain is the rectangle (0, 1.0) x (0, 0.20) in metres.
Generate a uniform structured mesh with 20 subdivisions in the x-direction and 4 subdivisions in the y-direction using dolfin.RectangleMesh.
Define the displacement space as a vector-valued degree-1 Lagrange (P1) space on the triangular mesh.
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law with the 2D Lamé parameters lambda_2D = E*nu/((1+nu)*(1-nu)) and mu = E/(2*(1+nu)), where E = 200e9 Pa and nu = 0.30.
Assemble the bilinear form a(u, v) = integral(sigma(u):strain(v))*dx over the domain using the 2D stress-strain relation sigma = lambda_2D*tr(strain(u))*I + 2*mu*strain(u).
The linear form b(v) is zero because the only loaded edges carry prescribed displacements and the top and bottom edges are traction-free.
Apply the Dirichlet boundary condition u = (0, 0) on the left edge x = 0.
Apply the Dirichlet boundary condition u = (0.001, 0) on the right edge x = 1.0.
Leave the top edge y = 0.20 and the bottom edge y = 0 unconstrained (natural, traction-free boundary conditions).
Solve the assembled linear system using a direct solver.
Post-process the solution by extracting the u_x component and rendering a filled colour-map (pcolormesh or equivalent) of u_x over the domain.
Save that colour-map figure to the file q1_ux.png.
Save the full vector displacement field to an XDMF file using dolfin.XDMFFile, writing the solution at time t = 0.
